objects.definition: typedef struct spng_ctx spng_ctx;
objects.description: Opaque spng context handle for decoding/encoding PNGs. Actual struct definition is hidden; manage via API. Must be created and freed with spng_ctx_new/spng_ctx_free.

objects.definition: typedef int spng_read_fn(spng_ctx *ctx, void *user, void *dest, size_t length);
objects.description: User-provided read callback signature for input streams.

objects.definition: typedef int spng_write_fn(spng_ctx *ctx, void *user, void *src, size_t length);
objects.description: User-provided write callback signature for output streams.

objects.definition: typedef int spng_rw_fn(spng_ctx *ctx, void *user, void *dst_src, size_t length);
objects.description: Generic read/write callback signature used by spng_set_png_stream.

functions.name: spng_ctx_new
functions.description: Creates a new spng context for decoding and/or encoding PNG images. Pass flags from spng_ctx_flags to configure behavior (e.g., SPNG_CTX_ENCODER for an encoder context). Returns a pointer to the new context or NULL on failure.
requirements: flags must be a valid combination of spng_ctx_flags
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle allocation failure
The returned spng_ctx* must be freed with spng_ctx_free

functions.name: spng_ctx_new2
functions.description: Creates a new spng context using custom memory allocation callbacks (alloc) and context flags. Use when you need custom malloc/realloc/calloc/free.
requirements: alloc may be NULL to use default allocation; if non-NULL, its function pointers must be valid for the duration of the context
flags must be a valid combination of spng_ctx_flags
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle allocation failure
The returned spng_ctx* must be freed with spng_ctx_free

functions.name: spng_ctx_free
functions.description: Destroys and frees a spng context created by spng_ctx_new/spng_ctx_new2, releasing all associated resources.
requirements: ctx may be NULL (no-op) or a valid spng_ctx* obtained from spng_ctx_new/spng_ctx_new2
After calling, the ctx pointer must not be used again

functions.name: spng_set_png_buffer
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_set_png_buffer(spng_ctx *ctx, const void *buf, size_t size);
functions.description: Associates an in-memory PNG byte buffer as the source (for decoding) or destination (when encoding to buffer) for the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least size bytes when used as input
size must be the total size of the PNG data buffer
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_png_stream
functions.description: Sets a user-supplied read/write callback for streaming PNG data. Useful for custom I/O sources/sinks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
rw_func must be a valid function pointer matching spng_rw_fn and must remain valid for the lifetime of I/O
user is an opaque pointer passed to rw_func; may be NULL
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_png_file
functions.description: Sets a stdio FILE* as the PNG data source or destination for the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
file must be a valid, open FILE* positioned appropriately for reading/ writing PNG data
The FILE* must remain valid while the context performs I/O
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_png_buffer
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to an internal PNG output buffer and its length after encoding when configured to encode to a buffer. On error, sets error code via error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
len should be a non-NULL pointer to receive the buffer length
error may be NULL or a pointer to receive an spng_errno
Returned pointer is managed by the library; callers must not free it unless the library specifies otherwise (unknown from header)
Caller must check error (if provided) and/or other API to confirm success

functions.name: spng_set_image_limits
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_set_image_limits(spng_ctx *ctx, uint32_t width, uint32_t height);
functions.description: Sets maximum allowed image dimensions for safety checks during decode/encode.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
width and height specify maximums; must be positive values within uint32_t range
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_image_limits
functions.description: Retrieves the current maximum allowed image width and height limits configured for the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
width and height must be non-NULL pointers to receive values
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_chunk_limits
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_set_chunk_limits(spng_ctx *ctx, size_t chunk_size, size_t cache_size);
functions.description: Sets safety limits for maximum chunk size and chunk cache size processed by the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
chunk_size and cache_size specify limits and must be reasonable size_t values
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_chunk_limits
functions.description: Retrieves the current chunk size and chunk cache limits for the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
chunk_size and cache_size must be non-NULL pointers to receive values
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_crc_action
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_set_crc_action(spng_ctx *ctx, int critical, int ancillary);
functions.description: Configures how CRC errors are handled for critical and ancillary chunks (SPNG_CRC_ERROR, SPNG_CRC_DISCARD, SPNG_CRC_USE).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
critical and ancillary must be one of enum spng_crc_action values
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_option
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_set_option(spng_ctx *ctx, enum spng_option option, int value);
functions.description: Sets a context option such as compression parameters, filter choices, unknown chunk handling, and others.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
option must be a valid enum spng_option value
value must be appropriate for the specified option (exact ranges unknown from header)
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_option
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_get_option(spng_ctx *ctx, enum spng_option option, int *value);
functions.description: Retrieves the current value for a given context option.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
option must be a valid enum spng_option value
value must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the option value
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_decoded_image_size
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_decoded_image_size(spng_ctx *ctx, int fmt, size_t *len);
functions.description: Calculates the number of bytes required to hold the decoded image in the specified output format (e.g., SPNG_FMT_RGBA8).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
fmt must be one of enum spng_format values
len must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the size
Context must have enough image metadata available to compute size (e.g., IHDR known); exact prerequisites unknown
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_decode_image
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_decode_image(spng_ctx *ctx, void *out, size_t len, int fmt, int flags);
functions.description: Decodes the PNG image to a caller-provided buffer in the specified output format. Supports optional flags (e.g., SPNG_DECODE_GAMMA, SPNG_DECODE_TRNS).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* with a PNG source configured via set_png_buffer/stream/file
out must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes
len should match or exceed the size returned by spng_decoded_image_size for the chosen fmt
fmt must be one of enum spng_format values
flags must be a valid combination of enum spng_decode_flags
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_decode_scanline
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_decode_scanline(spng_ctx *ctx, void *out, size_t len);
functions.description: Progressively decodes the next scanline into the provided buffer. Use after initializing progressive decode.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* configured for progressive decoding (SPNG_DECODE_PROGRESSIVE)
out must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes sized for one scanline in the chosen format (format selection method unspecified here)
Must be called in sequence for each scanline; ordering matters
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_decode_row
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_decode_row(spng_ctx *ctx, void *out, size_t len);
functions.description: Progressively decodes the next (possibly deinterlaced) row into the provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* configured for progressive decoding
out must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes for one output row
Must be called in sequence following the progressive decode protocol
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_decode_chunks
functions.description: Progressively processes non-image PNG chunks as part of progressive decoding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* configured for progressive decoding
Call in the correct order relative to scanline/row decoding as required by the progressive API (exact sequencing not specified in header)
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_row_info
functions.description: Retrieves information about the current row/scanline during progressive decode/encode (indexes, pass, filter).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
row_info must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_row_info struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_encode_image
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_encode_image(spng_ctx *ctx, const void *img, size_t len, int fmt, int flags);
functions.description: Encodes an image from a caller-provided buffer in the specified input format to PNG. Can optionally finalize the PNG or run progressively depending on flags.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* created with SPNG_CTX_ENCODER and configured with output (buffer/stream/file)
IHDR and other required PNG metadata must be set appropriately before encoding (details not in header)
img must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes
fmt must be one of enum spng_format values supported for encoding
flags must be a valid combination of enum spng_encode_flags
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_encode_scanline
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_encode_scanline(spng_ctx *ctx, const void *scanline, size_t len);
functions.description: Progressively encodes the next scanline from the caller-provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* created with SPNG_CTX_ENCODER and configured for progressive encoding (SPNG_ENCODE_PROGRESSIVE)
scanline must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes sized for one scanline in the specified input format
Calls must follow the correct order for progressive encoding
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_encode_row
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_encode_row(spng_ctx *ctx, const void *row, size_t len);
functions.description: Progressively encodes the next row (considering interlacing) from the caller-provided buffer.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* created with SPNG_CTX_ENCODER and configured for progressive encoding
row must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes for one row
Calls must follow correct row order per the progressive API
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_encode_chunks
functions.description: Progressively writes queued non-image chunks during encoding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* created with SPNG_CTX_ENCODER (typically with SPNG_ENCODE_PROGRESSIVE)
Calls must be sequenced correctly relative to scanline/row encoding
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_ihdr
functions.description: Reads the IHDR chunk fields (image header) from the context into ihdr.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
ihdr must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_ihdr struct
Context must have IHDR available (decoded or set); exact prerequisites unknown
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_plte
functions.description: Retrieves the PLTE (palette) chunk into plte.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
plte must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_plte struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_trns
functions.description: Retrieves the tRNS (transparency) chunk into trns.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
trns must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_trns struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_chrm
functions.description: Retrieves the cHRM chromaticity data as floating-point values.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
chrm must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_chrm struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_chrm_int
functions.description: Retrieves the cHRM chromaticity data as integer values (scaled).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
chrm_int must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_chrm_int struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_gama
functions.description: Retrieves the gAMA chunk as a floating-point gamma value.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
gamma must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the value
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_gama_int
functions.description: Retrieves the raw gAMA integer value as stored in the file.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
gama_int must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the value
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_iccp
functions.description: Retrieves the iCCP (ICC profile) chunk information, including profile name and data pointer/length.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
iccp must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_iccp struct
Returned profile pointer ownership/lifetime are library-defined; freeing rules unknown from header
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_sbit
functions.description: Retrieves the sBIT (significant bits) chunk.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
sbit must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_sbit struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_srgb
functions.description: Retrieves the sRGB chunk rendering intent.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
rendering_intent must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the value
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_text
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_get_text(spng_ctx *ctx, struct spng_text *text, uint32_t *n_text);
functions.description: Retrieves text chunks (tEXt, zTXt, iTXt). If text is NULL, n_text can be used to query the number of entries (usage pattern inferred).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
text and n_text must be valid pointers suitable for reading/writing as per usage; at minimum, n_text must be non-NULL to know count
Memory ownership of returned text buffers is library-defined; freeing rules unknown from header
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_bkgd
functions.description: Retrieves the bKGD (background color) chunk.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
bkgd must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_bkgd struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_hist
functions.description: Retrieves the hIST (histogram) chunk.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
hist must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_hist struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_phys
functions.description: Retrieves the pHYs (physical pixel dimensions) chunk.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
phys must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_phys struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_splt
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_get_splt(spng_ctx *ctx, struct spng_splt *splt, uint32_t *n_splt);
functions.description: Retrieves sPLT (suggested palette) chunks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
splt and n_splt must be valid pointers; at minimum, n_splt must be non-NULL to know count
Memory ownership of returned entries is library-defined; freeing rules unknown from header
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_time
functions.description: Retrieves the tIME (modification time) chunk.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
time must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_time struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_unknown_chunks
functions.signature: SPNG_API int spng_get_unknown_chunks(spng_ctx *ctx, struct spng_unknown_chunk *chunks, uint32_t *n_chunks);
functions.description: Retrieves unknown/unrecognized chunks preserved by the library.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
chunks and n_chunks must be valid pointers; at minimum, n_chunks must be non-NULL to know count
Memory ownership/lifetime for chunk data pointers is library-defined; freeing rules unknown from header
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_offs
functions.description: Retrieves the oFFs (image offset) chunk.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
offs must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_offs struct
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_get_exif
functions.description: Retrieves the eXIf chunk (EXIF metadata).
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx*
exif must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable spng_exif struct
Memory ownership of exif->data is library-defined; freeing rules unknown from header
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_ihdr
functions.description: Sets the IHDR (image header) fields for encoding or for overriding defaults prior to decode operations that need it.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (for encoding, created with SPNG_CTX_ENCODER)
ihdr must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized spng_ihdr
ihdr fields must conform to PNG spec ranges (exact validation rules not present in header)
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_plte
functions.description: Sets the PLTE (palette) chunk for encoding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
plte must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized spng_plte
PLTE must satisfy PNG constraints (e.g., entry count and relation to color type); exact rules not specified here
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_trns
functions.description: Sets the tRNS (transparency) chunk for encoding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
trns must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized spng_trns
tRNS constraints depend on color type and PLTE presence; exact rules not specified here
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_chrm
functions.description: Sets the cHRM chromaticity chunk using floating-point values.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
chrm must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized spng_chrm
Values must be within valid ranges per PNG spec; exact limits not specified here
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_chrm_int
functions.description: Sets the cHRM chromaticity chunk using integer (scaled) values.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
chrm_int must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized spng_chrm_int
Values must be within valid ranges per PNG spec; exact limits not specified here
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_gama
functions.description: Sets the gAMA chunk as a floating-point gamma value.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
gamma must be a positive value within valid range for PNG (exact range not specified here)
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_gama_int
functions.description: Sets the raw gAMA integer value.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
gamma must be a valid PNG gAMA integer (exact constraints not specified here)
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates an spng_errno

functions.name: spng_set_iccp
functions.description: Sets the iCCP (ICC profile) chunk for encoding.
requirements: ctx must be a valid spng_ctx* (encoder context for writing)
iccp must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized spng_iccp with profile name, length, and data pointer

import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator creates small but valid PNG files exercising a variety of
# chunks that the fuzzers read: IHDR, PLTE, tRNS, gAMA, cHRM, sRGB, pHYs, tEXt,
# sPLT, tIME, oFFs, eXIf, iCCP, and unknown chunks, with actual IDAT image data.
# The output stays <= 4096 bytes and varies with the seed.

# PNG helpers
PNG_SIG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"


def crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def chunk(typ: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + typ + data + struct.pack(">I", crc32(typ + data))


# Build various ancillary chunks with valid encodings

def make_IHDR(width: int, height: int, bit_depth: int, color_type: int, interlace: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # compression=0, filter=0 per PNG spec
    data = struct.pack(
        ">IIBBBBB",
        width,
        height,
        bit_depth,
        color_type,
        0,  # compression
        0,  # filter
        interlace,
    )
    return chunk(b"IHDR", data)


def paeth_predict(a, b, c):
    p = a + b - c
    pa = abs(p - a)
    pb = abs(p - b)
    pc = abs(p - c)
    if pa <= pb and pa <= pc:
        return a
    elif pb <= pc:
        return b
    else:
        return c


def filter_scanline(raw: bytes, bpp: int, method: int) -> bytes:
    # method: 0 None, 1 Sub, 2 Up, 3 Average, 4 Paeth. We generate valid filters.
    if method == 0:
        return bytes([0]) + raw
    out = bytearray(len(raw))
    if method == 1:  # Sub
        for i in range(len(raw)):
            left = out[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
            out[i] = (raw[i] - left) & 0xFF
        return bytes([1]) + bytes(out)
    elif method == 2:  # Up (assuming previous row zeros)
        for i in range(len(raw)):
            out[i] = (raw[i] - 0) & 0xFF
        return bytes([2]) + bytes(out)
    elif method == 3:  # Average (prev=0)
        for i in range(len(raw)):
            left = out[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
            up = 0
            out[i] = (raw[i] - ((left + up) // 2)) & 0xFF
        return bytes([3]) + bytes(out)
    elif method == 4:  # Paeth (prev=0)
        for i in range(len(raw)):
            left = out[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
            up = 0
            upleft = 0
            pr = paeth_predict(left, up, upleft)
            out[i] = (raw[i] - pr) & 0xFF
        return bytes([4]) + bytes(out)
    else:
        return bytes([0]) + raw


def interlace_adam7_passes(w: int, h: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
    # Returns list of (x_start, y_start, x_step, y_step)
    return [
        (0, 0, 8, 8),
        (4, 0, 8, 8),
        (0, 4, 4, 8),
        (2, 0, 4, 4),
        (0, 2, 2, 4),
        (1, 0, 2, 2),
        (0, 1, 1, 2),
    ]


def build_IDAT_rgba8(w: int, h: int, rng: random.Random, interlace: int = 0, filter_method: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Build deterministic but varied content: gradients + stripes
    # RGBA8: 4 bytes per pixel
    def pixel(x, y):
        r = (x * 7 + y * 13) & 0xFF
        g = (x * 17 + y * 5) & 0xFF
        b = (x * 3 + y * 29) & 0xFF
        a = 255
        return bytes([r, g, b, a])

    bpp = 4
    filtered_rows = []
    if interlace == 0:
        for y in range(h):
            row = bytearray()
            for x in range(w):
                row += pixel(x, y)
            method = filter_method if filter_method in (0, 1, 2, 3, 4) else 0
            # randomize per-row a bit
            if filter_method == 255:
                method = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4])
            filtered_rows.append(filter_scanline(bytes(row), bpp, method))
    else:
        # Adam7 interlace; for each pass, construct subimage rows
        passes = interlace_adam7_passes(w, h)
        for (xs, ys, dx, dy) in passes:
            # determine pass width and height
            pw = (w - xs + dx - 1) // dx if w > xs else 0
            ph = (h - ys + dy - 1) // dy if h > ys else 0
            if pw <= 0 or ph <= 0:
                continue
            for py in range(ph):
                row = bytearray()
                y = ys + py * dy
                for px in range(pw):
                    x = xs + px * dx
                    row += pixel(x, y)
                method = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4])
                filtered_rows.append(filter_scanline(bytes(row), bpp, method))
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level=rng.choice([0, 1, 3, 6, 9]))
    data = comp.compress(b"".join(filtered_rows)) + comp.flush()
    return chunk(b"IDAT", data)


def make_PLTE_and_tRNS_for_indexed(n: int, include_trns: bool, rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    n = max(1, min(256, n))
    pl = bytearray()
    tr = bytearray()
    trns_len = rng.randrange(1, n + 1) if include_trns else 0
    for i in range(n):
        r = (i * 53) & 0xFF
        g = (i * 97) & 0xFF
        b = (i * 199) & 0xFF
        pl += bytes([r, g, b])
        if i < trns_len:
            tr.append(255 if i % 7 else 0)
    plte = chunk(b"PLTE", bytes(pl))
    trns = chunk(b"tRNS", bytes(tr)) if trns_len > 0 else b""
    return plte, trns


def make_gAMA(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # store as integer g = round(gamma*100000). Choose common 45455 (~2.2) or random in range
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        g = 45455
    else:
        g = rng.randint(10000, 80000)
    return chunk(b"gAMA", struct.pack(">I", g))


def make_cHRM(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Use sRGB-ish integers (scaled by 100000): wp (31270,32900), r(64000,33000), g(30000,60000), b(15000,6000)
    vals = [31270, 32900, 64000, 33000, 30000, 60000, 15000, 6000]
    # Occasionally vary slightly
    vals = [max(1, v + rng.randint(-200, 200)) for v in vals]
    data = b"".join(struct.pack(">I", v) for v in vals)
    return chunk(b"cHRM", data)


def make_sRGB(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    intent = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3])
    return chunk(b"sRGB", bytes([intent]))


def make_pHYs(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # pixels per unit; choose 2835 (72 DPI) or 3780 (96 DPI)
    ppu_x = rng.choice([2835, 3780, 11811])
    ppu_y = rng.choice([2835, 3780, 11811])
    unit = rng.choice([0, 1])  # 0=unknown, 1=meters
    return chunk(b"pHYs", struct.pack(">IIB", ppu_x, ppu_y, unit))


def make_tEXt(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # keyword up to 79 bytes ASCII, non-empty, no nulls; then null, then text
    kw_choices = [b"Comment", b"Author", b"Title", b"Description", b"Software"]
    keyword = rng.choice(kw_choices)
    text = ("Generated by seed %d" % rng.randint(0, 1_000_000)).encode("ascii")
    return chunk(b"tEXt", keyword + b"\x00" + text)


def make_tIME(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    year = rng.randint(1990, 2030)
    month = rng.randint(1, 12)
    day = rng.randint(1, 28)
    hour = rng.randint(0, 23)
    minute = rng.randint(0, 59)
    second = rng.randint(0, 59)
    return chunk(b"tIME", struct.pack(">HBBBBB", year, month, day, hour, minute, second))


def make_oFFs(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    x = rng.randint(-10000, 10000)
    y = rng.randint(-10000, 10000)
    unit = rng.choice([0, 1])
    return chunk(b"oFFs", struct.pack(">iiB", x, y, unit))


def make_eXIf(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal EXIF header: TIFF little-endian header (II*\x00), 0th IFD with 0 entries
    exif_header = b"Exif\x00\x00"
    tiff_le = b"II" + b"*\x00" + struct.pack("<I", 8) + struct.pack("<H", 0) + struct.pack("<I", 0)
    data = exif_header + tiff_le
    return chunk(b"eXIf", data)


def make_iCCP(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Profile name: ASCII up to 79; compression method=0; compressed profile follows.
    name = rng.choice([b"sRGB IEC61966-2.1", b"Generic RGB", b"Display P3"]).split(b"\x00")[0][:79]
    comp_method = b"\x00"
    # Use small dummy ICC content (valid zlib stream). ICC content itself isn't validated deeply by libspng.
    raw_profile = b"ICC_PROFILE" + bytes([rng.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(rng.randint(16, 64))])
    comp = zlib.compress(raw_profile, level=rng.choice([1, 6, 9]))
    data = name + b"\x00" + comp_method + comp
    return chunk(b"iCCP", data)


def make_sPLT(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # sPLT name, sample depth, entries (8 or 16-bit)
    name = rng.choice([b"spalette", b"alt", b"ui"])[:79]
    depth8 = rng.choice([True, False])
    n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    if depth8:
        entries = bytearray()
        for i in range(n):
            r = (i * 31) & 0xFF
            g = (i * 57) & 0xFF
            b = (i * 83) & 0xFF
            a = (200 + i) & 0xFF
            freq = rng.randint(0, 65535)
            entries += bytes([r, g, b, a]) + struct.pack(">H", freq)
        data = name + b"\x00" + bytes([8]) + bytes(entries)
    else:
        entries = bytearray()
        for i in range(n):
            r = (i * 257 * 31) & 0xFFFF
            g = (i * 257 * 57) & 0xFFFF
            b = (i * 257 * 83) & 0xFFFF
            a = (50000 + i * 17) & 0xFFFF
            freq = rng.randint(0, 65535)
            entries += struct.pack(">HHHHH", r, g, b, a, freq)
        data = name + b"\x00" + bytes([16]) + bytes(entries)
    return chunk(b"sPLT", data)


def make_unknown(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # type must be 4 ASCII letters; avoid critical known ones but keep valid range
    letters = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    t = bytes([rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(4)])
    # Ensure ancillary by setting lowercase 5th bit in first char: set bit 5 to 1
    t = bytes([t[0] | 0x20]) + t[1:]
    payload = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 16)))
    return chunk(t, payload)


def assemble_png(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose color type and bit depth combos that are widely supported
    # Prefer RGBA8 to exercise decode paths that convert formats.
    color_choice = rng.choices(
        population=[(6, 8), (2, 8), (3, 8)],
        weights=[6, 3, 2],
        k=1,
    )[0]
    color_type, bit_depth = color_choice

    # Small dimensions to keep buffer tiny but non-trivial
    width = rng.randint(8, 64)
    height = rng.randint(8, 64)

    interlace = rng.choice([0, 1]) if (width * height <= 2048) else 0

    parts: List[bytes] = [PNG_SIG]

    # Sometimes include sRGB/gAMA/cHRM combinations
    # Per spec: If sRGB present, gAMA and cHRM should match sRGB; decoders generally accept them in practice.

    # Build PLTE/tRNS if indexed
    ancillary_pre: List[bytes] = []
    if color_type == 3:
        npl = rng.randint(2, 16)
        include_trns = rng.random() < 0.7
        plte, trns = make_PLTE_and_tRNS_for_indexed(npl, include_trns, rng)
        ancillary_pre.extend([plte])
        if trns:
            ancillary_pre.append(trns)

    # Common global ancillary chunks
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_tEXt(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_pHYs(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_tIME(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_oFFs(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_eXIf(rng))
    # Color-related chunks
    color_chunks = []
    style = rng.choice(["srgb", "gamma_chrm", "none"]) if color_type != 3 else rng.choice(["srgb", "gamma_chrm"])  # keep interesting
    if style == "srgb":
        color_chunks.append(make_sRGB(rng))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            color_chunks.append(make_gAMA(rng))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            color_chunks.append(make_cHRM(rng))
    elif style == "gamma_chrm":
        color_chunks.append(make_gAMA(rng))
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            color_chunks.append(make_cHRM(rng))

    # Optional iCCP
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        color_chunks.append(make_iCCP(rng))

    # Optional sPLT and unknown
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_sPLT(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ancillary_pre.append(make_unknown(rng))

    # IHDR
    parts.append(make_IHDR(width, height, bit_depth, color_type, interlace))

    # Place PLTE/tRNS and color chunks appropriately before IDAT
    parts.extend(ancillary_pre)
    parts.extend(color_chunks)

    # Image data
    if color_type in (2, 6):
        # truecolor or truecolor+alpha -> generate RGBA8 then convert if needed
        filt_mode = 255 if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4])
        idat = build_IDAT_rgba8(width, height, rng, interlace=interlace, filter_method=filt_mode)
        parts.append(idat)
    elif color_type == 3:
        # Indexed color: build an indexed image with simple patterns and compress
        # Sample depth 8 for simplicity
        # Build scanlines: one-byte per pixel indices
        def idx(x, y):
            return (x + y * 3) % 16
        rows = []
        for y in range(height):
            raw = bytearray((idx(x, y) for x in range(width)))
            # filter type 0 for simplicity
            rows.append(bytes([0]) + bytes(raw))
        comp = zlib.compressobj(level=rng.choice([1, 6, 9]))
        data = comp.compress(b"".join(rows)) + comp.flush()
        parts.append(chunk(b"IDAT", data))
    else:
        # Fallback to a minimal valid single black row RGBA transformed; but we chose from supported set
        parts.append(build_IDAT_rgba8(width, height, rng))

    # Optional more unknown after IDAT to exercise get_unknown_chunks location after IDAT
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(make_unknown(rng))

    # IEND
    parts.append(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

    png = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(png) > 4096:
        # Trim by removing some optional chunks; keep core valid structure
        keep = [PNG_SIG, parts[1]]  # signature + IHDR
        # Keep first ancillary up to some limit
        budget = 4096 - len(b"".join(keep)) - len(chunk(b"IDAT", b"")) - len(chunk(b"IEND", b"")) - 128
        size_acc = 0
        for p in parts[2:-2]:
            if size_acc + len(p) <= budget:
                keep.append(p)
                size_acc += len(p)
        keep.append(parts[-2])  # IDAT
        keep.append(parts[-1])  # IEND
        png = b"".join(keep)
    return png


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_png(rng)

# This generator targets spng_set_iccp, spng_set_text, and spng_set_splt fuzzers.
# It needs to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) with valid, interesting data.
# We produce a single bytes buffer that concatenates multiple ASCII strings and 32-bit integers
# so that different FUZZ_PARAM_* calls will draw sequentially and receive sensible values.
#
# Design:
# - Strings: ASCII, alphanumeric with some safe punctuation, lengths tailored to PNG limits.
#   We include a mix of lengths: small, typical, and near maximum (e.g., 79 for names/keywords, 1024 for payloads).
# - Integers: 32-bit values chosen to exercise branches: picking text types (1,2,3), depths (8/16), counts, flags.
# - Order independence: Although the fuzzer requests parameters in an unknown sequence, we
#   interleave enough strings and integers so most sequences find suitable values.
# - Size capped below 4096 bytes.
#
# Encoding format of this buffer (self-describing):
# [u32 count_str][repeated: u16 len + bytes str][u32 count_int][repeated: u32 int]
# The harness will not parse this, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) in the fuzzing
# framework usually read sequentially from the buffer; a simple length-prefixed layout ensures
# strings are contiguous and varied. If the framework simply slices bytes, the ASCII content still
# forms valid strings, and u32 words provide diverse integers.

SAFE_PUNCT = "-_ ./:+,()[]{}"
ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
ASCII_POOL = ALNUM + SAFE_PUNCT

# Helpers to craft domain-specific interesting strings

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure starts with alnum to be a valid PNG keyword/name start
    if n == 0:
        return ""
    s = rng.choice(ALNUM)
    if n > 1:
        s += "".join(rng.choice(ASCII_POOL) for _ in range(n - 1))
    # Strip forbidden NUL implicitly by never generating it
    # Trim trailing spaces (PNG keywords disallow leading/trailing spaces)
    return s.strip() or "k"

# Common near-limit sizes for PNG metadata
KEYWORD_MAX = 79
PROFILE_NAME_MAX = 79
TEXT_MAX = 1024
LANG_MAX = 64

# Pre-build some canonical values to increase validity
CANON_KEYWORDS = [
    "Author", "Description", "Title", "Software", "Comment", "Copyright",
    "Disclaimer", "Source", "CreationTime", "Warning"
]
CANON_LANG = ["en", "en-US", "fr", "de", "es", "zh", "ja", "ru", "pt-BR", "ar"]
CANON_NAMES = ["sRGB IEC61966-2.1", "Display P3", "AdobeRGB1998", "ProPhotoRGB", "MyICCProfile"]


def build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    strs: List[bytes] = []

    # For iCCP profile name (<=79)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            name = rng.choice(CANON_NAMES)
        else:
            name = rand_ascii(rng, 1, PROFILE_NAME_MAX)
        strs.append(name[:PROFILE_NAME_MAX].encode('ascii', 'ignore'))

    # For iCCP profile payload (~1KB typical)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        # Build readable ASCII payload of varying sizes 128..1024
        size = rng.choice([128, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024])
        payload = (rand_ascii(rng, 8, 16) + " ")
        block = (payload * (size // max(1, len(payload))))[:size]
        strs.append(block.encode('ascii', 'ignore'))

    # For text keywords (<=79) and payloads (<=1024)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            kw = rng.choice(CANON_KEYWORDS)
        else:
            kw = rand_ascii(rng, 1, KEYWORD_MAX)
        strs.append(kw[:KEYWORD_MAX].encode('ascii', 'ignore'))
        # payload of various lengths
        tlen = rng.choice([1, 8, 32, 128, 512, 1024])
        txt = "".join(rng.choice(ASCII_POOL) for _ in range(tlen))
        if not txt:
            txt = "x"
        strs.append(txt.encode('ascii', 'ignore'))
        # iTXt language tag and translated keyword
        lang = rng.choice(CANON_LANG) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rand_ascii(rng, 2, LANG_MAX)
        strs.append(lang[:LANG_MAX].encode('ascii', 'ignore'))
        trkw = rand_ascii(rng, 1, LANG_MAX)
        strs.append(trkw[:LANG_MAX].encode('ascii', 'ignore'))

    # For sPLT names (<=79)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        nm = rand_ascii(rng, 1, PROFILE_NAME_MAX)
        strs.append(nm[:PROFILE_NAME_MAX].encode('ascii', 'ignore'))

    return strs


def build_ints(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    ints: List[int] = []

    # Text types: 1,2,3; compression flag 0/1; method 0
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)):
        ints.append(rng.choice([1, 2, 3]))  # type
        ints.append(rng.choice([0, 1]))     # compression_flag
        # A few arbitrary ints for framework consumption
        ints.append(0)  # compression_method always 0 for zlib

    # sPLT depths 8/16 and entry counts 1..8
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        ints.append(rng.choice([8, 16]))
        ints.append(rng.randint(1, 8))

    # Frequencies and channel values boundaries for sPLT entries
    # Provide plenty of 8-bit and 16-bit boundary values
    boundary_vals_8 = [0, 1, 127, 128, 254, 255]
    boundary_vals_16 = [0, 1, 255, 256, 32767, 32768, 65534, 65535]
    for _ in range(40):
        ints.append(rng.choice(boundary_vals_8))
        ints.append(rng.choice(boundary_vals_16))

    # Flags for set_text array count selection in fuzzer (1..3)
    for _ in range(6):
        ints.append(rng.randint(1, 3))

    # Extra general-purpose 32-bit ints to satisfy any additional FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    for _ in range(32):
        ints.append(rng.getrandbits(32))

    return ints


def pack_u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(n >> 8) & 0xFF, n & 0xFF])


def pack_u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([
        (n >> 24) & 0xFF,
        (n >> 16) & 0xFF,
        (n >> 8) & 0xFF,
        n & 0xFF,
    ])


def serialize(strings: List[bytes], ints: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # Length-prefix strings with u16, guard max 2048
    out = bytearray()
    out += pack_u32(len(strings))
    for s in strings:
        s = s[:2048]
        out += pack_u16(len(s))
        out += s
    out += pack_u32(len(ints))
    for v in ints:
        out += pack_u32(v & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings = build_strings(rng)
    ints = build_ints(rng)
    buf = serialize(strings, ints)

    # Ensure upper bound size
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for a binary blob to feed spng fuzzers that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME.
# Targets:
# - spng_set_iccp: ICC profile name (<=79, non-empty) and binary profile payload (<=1024 suggested)
# - spng_set_text: keywords (<=79), type {1,2,3}, text payloads, iTXt fields (lang/tag, translated keyword)
# - spng_set_unknown_chunks: 1..2 chunks, 4-byte type, small data (<=256), location {1,2,8}
# - spng_set_exif: EXIF blob up to ~1KB
#
# We build a structured byte buffer of length-prefixed fields so that
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls get reasonable, valid-looking inputs.

PRINTABLE = bytes([c for c in range(0x20, 0x7F)])
ALNUM = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
UPPER = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int, printable_bias: float = 0.8) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        if r.random() < printable_bias:
            out.append(r.choice(PRINTABLE))
        else:
            out.append(r.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(out)

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(n))

def _len_prefixed(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>H', len(data)) + data

def _mk_keyword(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    l = r.randint(1, max_len)
    s = bytearray()
    for i in range(l):
        if i > 0 and r.random() < 0.15:
            s.append(0x20)
        else:
            s.append(r.choice(ALNUM))
    while s and s[-1] == 0x20:
        s.pop()
    if not s:
        s = bytearray(b"K")
    return bytes(s[:max_len])

def _mk_lang_tag(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # RFC-like language tag: 1-3 parts of 2-3 alpha chars, lowercase, joined by '-'
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        part = _rand_ascii(r, r.randint(2, 3)).lower()
        parts.append(part)
    tag = b"-".join(parts) if parts else b"en"
    return tag[:max_len] if tag else b"en"

def _mk_chunk_type(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.choice(UPPER) for _ in range(4))

def _mk_icc_name(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    l = r.randint(1, 79)
    return _rand_ascii(r, l)

def _mk_icc_profile(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create an ICC-like blob: include size and "acsp" magic at offset 36
    size = r.randint(64, 512)
    buf = bytearray(size)
    struct.pack_into('>I', buf, 0, size)
    buf[4:8] = b"pyth"
    buf[8:12] = b"\x04\x00\x00\x00"
    buf[12:16] = b"mntr"
    buf[16:20] = b"RGB "
    buf[20:24] = b"XYZ "
    for off in range(24, 36):
        buf[off] = r.randrange(0, 256)
    buf[36:40] = b"acsp"
    for i in range(40, size):
        buf[i] = r.randrange(0, 256)
    return bytes(buf)

def _mk_text_payload(r: random.Random, ttype: int) -> bytes:
    l = r.randint(0, 256 if ttype == 1 else 512)
    return _rand_bytes(r, l, printable_bias=0.95)

def _mk_unknown_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    l = r.randint(0, 200)
    return _rand_bytes(r, l, printable_bias=0.6)

def _mk_exif_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    endian_le = r.random() < 0.5
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"II" if endian_le else b"MM"
    header += b"\x2A\x00" if endian_le else b"\x00\x2A"
    header += b"\x08\x00\x00\x00" if endian_le else b"\x00\x00\x00\x08"
    header += b"\x00\x00"  # 0 entries
    header += b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"  # next IFD = 0
    trail = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 128), printable_bias=0.4)
    return bytes(header) + trail

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # spng_set_iccp: name, profile
    icc_name = _mk_icc_name(r)
    icc_prof = _mk_icc_profile(r)
    chunks.append(_len_prefixed(icc_name))
    chunks.append(_len_prefixed(icc_prof))

    # spng_set_text: 1..3 entries
    n_text = r.randint(1, 3)
    chunks.append(struct.pack('>B', n_text))
    for _ in range(n_text):
        keyword = _mk_keyword(r, 79)
        ttype = r.choice([1, 2, 3])
        text = _mk_text_payload(r, ttype)
        comp_flag = 1 if ttype == 3 and r.random() < 0.5 else 0
        lang = _mk_lang_tag(r, 64) if ttype == 3 else b""
        trkw = _mk_keyword(r, 64) if ttype == 3 else b""
        chunks.append(_len_prefixed(keyword))
        chunks.append(struct.pack('>B', ttype))
        chunks.append(_len_prefixed(text))
        chunks.append(struct.pack('>B', comp_flag))
        chunks.append(_len_prefixed(lang))
        chunks.append(_len_prefixed(trkw))

    # spng_set_unknown_chunks: 1..2 entries
    n_unk = r.randint(1, 2)
    chunks.append(struct.pack('>B', n_unk))
    for _ in range(n_unk):
        ctype = _mk_chunk_type(r)
        payload = _mk_unknown_payload(r)
        loc = r.choice([1, 2, 8])
        chunks.append(ctype)
        chunks.append(_len_prefixed(payload))
        chunks.append(struct.pack('>B', loc))

    # spng_set_exif: blob
    exif = _mk_exif_blob(r)
    chunks.append(_len_prefixed(exif))

    blob = b"SPNGFUZZ\x00" + b"".join(chunks)
    return blob[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a UTF-8 text blob intended to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the spng_set_text fuzzer.
# The fuzzer constructs 1..3 spng_text entries using multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls for:
# - keyword (1..79 ASCII/UTF-8, NUL-terminated by callee)
# - text payload (up to 1024)
# - language_tag (iTXt only, up to 64)
# - translated_keyword (iTXt only, up to 64)
# It also uses FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) multiple times for counts/types/flags. Those are not provided by this buffer
# but we provide a rich concatenation of strings so FUZZ_PARAM_STR has interesting, valid UTF-8 options.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build several concatenated UTF-8 strings separated by newlines, including:
#   * Valid PNG text keywords (ASCII 32..126 except disallowing control and ensuring non-empty)
#   * Language tags resembling BCP47 (e.g., en, en-US, zh-Hant-TW)
#   * Translated keywords using diverse Unicode scripts
#   * Text payloads of varying sizes, including long (<= 1024), multiline, with emojis, combined marks, and RTL text
# - Ensure overall buffer <= 4096 bytes
# - Randomize selection and sizes based on seed
#
# Consumers typically read FUZZ_PARAM_STR by slicing from a corpus entry or delimited store; providing multiple
# newline-separated entries increases chance that the harness will draw different meaningful strings.

ASCII_KEYWORD_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-+.,:;()[]{}#@!$%&^~"  # avoid tabs and control chars

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "Plain ASCII text",
    "Multiline\ntext with\nnewlines",
    "Emoji 😀😃😄😁😆😉😊😍🤖",
    "Combining a012 and e012",
    "Accents café naïve façade coöperate",
    "CJK: 漢字仮名交じり文とかなとカタカナ",
    "RTL: مرحبا بالعالم",
    "Hebrew: שלום עולם",
    "Thai: สวัสดีโลก",
    "Devanagari: नमस्ते दुनिया",
    "Surrogates test: 𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢 𝟙𝟚𝟛",
]

LANG_TAGS = [
    "en", "en-US", "en-GB",
    "fr", "fr-CA",
    "de-DE",
    "es", "es-419",
    "pt-BR", "pt-PT",
    "zh", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant-TW",
    "ja-JP",
    "ko-KR",
    "ru-RU",
    "ar-EG",
    "he-IL",
]

TRANSLATED_KEYWORDS = [
    "Title", "Author", "Description", "Software", "Comment",
    "タイトル", "作者", "説明",
    "标题", "作者", "描述",
    "Título", "Autor", "Descripción",
    "Описание", "Программное обеспечение",
    "وصف", "عنوان",
]

# Generate a valid PNG keyword: 1..79 bytes, printable, no NUL; typically ASCII
# PNG keyword rules: length 1..79, Latin-1 per spec; UTF-8 allowable in iTXt. We'll keep it simple ASCII printable.
def make_keyword(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(1, 79)
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces sometimes
    body = ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_KEYWORD_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    # Trim to avoid all-space
    if body.strip() == "":
        body = "k"
    return body

# Generate a language tag-like string <= 64 bytes
def make_lang_tag(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = rng.choice(LANG_TAGS)
    else:
        # Construct pseudo BCP47: ll[-Script][-REGION]
        ll = rng.choice(["en","fr","de","es","pt","zh","ja","ko","ru","ar","he","hi","th","tr","it"])
        script = rng.choice(["Latn","Cyrl","Hans","Hant","Jpan","Kore","Arab","Hebr"]) if rng.random() < 0.5 else None
        region = rng.choice(["US","GB","CA","BR","PT","CN","TW","JP","KR","RU","EG","IL","IN","TH","TR","IT"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else None
        parts = [ll]
        if script: parts.append(script)
        if region: parts.append(region)
        base = '-'.join(parts)
    # Ensure <= 64 bytes
    return base[:64]

# Generate translated keyword <= 64 bytes, often short
def make_translated_keyword(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        s = rng.choice(TRANSLATED_KEYWORDS)
    else:
        s = make_keyword(rng)
    return s[:64]

# Generate text payload up to 1024 bytes; include various features
def make_text_payload(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    chunks: List[str] = []
    # Ensure at least one from samples
    chunks.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
    # Optionally add repeated lines
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        rep = rng.randint(1, 5)
        line = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        chunks.extend([line] * rep)
    # Optionally add ASCII paragraph
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        words = [rng.choice(["PNG","libspng","metadata","iTXt","zTXt","tEXt","gamma","profile","palette","compression"]) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 30))]
        chunks.append(' '.join(words))
    # Optionally add emojis
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append("😀" * rng.randint(1, 50))
    # Optionally add long filler
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        filler = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ' _-.,;:/') for _ in range(rng.randint(50, 500)))
        chunks.append(filler)
    txt = "\n".join(chunks)
    # Truncate to 1024 bytes safely on codepoint boundary
    b = txt.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
        # ensure valid UTF-8: back up to start of a character if we cut inside
        while (b and (b[-1] & 0b11000000) == 0b10000000):
            b = b[:-1]
        try:
            txt = b.decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            # Fallback: remove last byte until valid
            while b:
                b = b[:-1]
                try:
                    txt = b.decode('utf-8')
                    break
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    continue
            else:
                txt = ""
    return txt

# Build a corpus of strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR to consume
# We separate entries by newlines; many fuzz harnesses split or use slices.
def build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []
    # Add several keywords
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        corpus.append(make_keyword(rng))
    # Add several language tags
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        corpus.append(make_lang_tag(rng))
    # Add several translated keywords
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        corpus.append(make_translated_keyword(rng))
    # Add multiple text payloads
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        corpus.append(make_text_payload(rng))
    # Add edge-case short strings
    corpus.extend(["k", "a", "0", "en", "Title"])  # very short
    # Add boundary-length strings (79-char keyword, 64-char tag)
    corpus.append(('K' * 79))
    corpus.append(('l' * 64))
    # Add empty? The fuzzer guards keyword empty by forcing 'k', but empty is fine for text/language fields
    corpus.append("")
    return corpus


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = build_corpus(rng)
    # Join with newline separators so consumer can slice multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    blob = "\n".join(corpus)
    b = blob.encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure <= 4096 bytes
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # ensure valid UTF-8
        while (b and (b[-1] & 0b11000000) == 0b10000000):
            b = b[:-1]
    return b
